cues: Light opens stomata, so transpiration rises.
A gentle breeze raises it by sweeping away humid air, but a strong wind makes stomata close.
And a thick cuticle, sunken stomata as in Nerium, or a coat of hairs, all cut water loss.
text: What changes the rate? Light opens stomata, so transpiration rises. Warmth raises it steeply. Humid air lowers it. A gentle breeze raises it by sweeping away humid air, but a strong wind makes stomata close. And a thick cuticle, sunken stomata as in Nerium, or a coat of hairs, all cut water loss.
